    Translation

    973- Junāda (first vowel ḍamma, then nūn) b. Abī Umayya al-Azdī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Shāmī, whose father's name was said to be Kabīr; disputed Companion status. Al-ʿIjlī called him a trustworthy Successor. The truth is that two men shared the same personal name and their fathers' kunya, one a Companion and the other a Successor, as I explained in my book on the Companions. Junāda al-Azdī's narration from the Prophet ﷺ occurs in al-Nasāʾī's Sunan, whereas Junāda b. Abī Umayya's narration from ʿUbāda b. al-Ṣāmit occurs in all six books. [all six]
